data.description: Patient on post-op day 2 following total knee arthroplasty developed severe uncontrolled pain (9/10) with hemodynamic instability (HR 117, BP 175/103), hypoxia (SpO2 91%), and fever (39.1C). Multimodal analgesia failed. Opioid escalation recommended but not administered due to administrative denial. Elevated troponin noted on BMP; cardiac workup negative on X-ray. No acute pulmonary process. Evidence of acute kidney injury (creatinine 1.8) and hyperkalemia (5.6 mEq/L). Drug interaction screen showed no major interactions. No clinical guideline available for refractory post-surgical pain (evidence level D).
interventions: Labs repeated with BMP showing metabolic abnormalities
Chest X-ray performed to rule out pulmonary cause
data.outcome: Clinical deterioration observed; recommended pharmacologic intervention not administered. Patient remains at high risk for complications including delirium, poor mobility, and prolonged recovery.

data.description: Pain management escalation attempted with high-dose hydromorphone and sufentanil despite abnormal vitals and lab results. Prescription requests denied by system due to safety concerns. Patient exhibited tachycardia, hypertension, hypoxia, fever, and acute kidney injury. No clinical guideline available for refractory post-surgical pain in this context.

Attempted prescription of hydromorphone 64mg IV Q2H and sufentanil 30mcg sublingual Q1H for refractory post-op pain in opioid-naive patient with atrial fibrillation. Dosing exceeds standard guidelines by 60-100x. Request originated from attending but flagged by clinical decision support. Action blocked by Admin phase oversight. No harm occurred due to intervention.
data.root_cause: Misinterpretation of 'exceptional tolerance' note; lack of standardized opioid conversion protocol
recommended_actions: Implement mandatory opioid conversion calculator in EHR
Require dual-physician approval for high-dose opioid initiation
Update triage protocols to flag patients with atrial fibrillation on high-dose opioids
